useful context, but not direct target-period conduct."},{"evidence_id":"E0003","reason":"Inherited treaty status; it supports baseline nonproliferation context, not Abiy-specific action."},{"evidence_id":"E0004","reason":"Inherited verification/treaty context; not evidence of a 2022 ruler decision."},{"evidence_id":"E0005","reason":"Regional treaty posture is context, not proof of Abiy's conduct in 2022."},{"evidence_id":"E0006","reason":"Current safeguards factsheet is structural context, not target-year conduct."},{"evidence_id":"E0007","reason":"Historical peaceful-use framework is background only and not a 2022 choice."},{"evidence_id":"E0008","reason":"Global nuclear-armed-state list is exposure context, not ruler-level evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0009","reason":"Conventional ceasefire/truce reporting; relevant to crisis management but not nuclear-risk governance."},{"evidence_id":"E0010","reason":"Peace-process context for conventional conflict, not a direct existential-risk decision."},{"evidence_id":"E0011","reason":"Conflict-resumption reporting is conventional-war context, not nuclear-risk conduct."},{"evidence_id":"E0012","reason":"Human-rights and humanitarian-crisis context; not a nuclear or catastrophic-risk decision record."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"No direct 2022 evidence of an Abiy-attributed nuclear, biological, cyber, or other existential-risk decision.","lenses":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.3","1B.8","1B.9","1B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Archived 2022 PMO, cabinet, defense, foreign-affairs, and IAEA/CTBTO records tied to Abiy's own statements or orders.","why_it_matters":"Without a ruler-specific risk-bearing act, the chapter is mostly inherited posture and conflict context."},{"gap":"Insufficient evidence on dual-use or catastrophic-risk governance beyond treaty baseline.","lenses":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"IAEA safeguards correspondence, national radiation-safety or biosafety/cyber policy records, and contemporaneous official directives.","why_it_matters":"The package does not show whether Abiy actually strengthened or weakened practical risk controls."}],"reason":"The dossier is honest about Ethiopia's non-nuclear baseline and Abiy's limited exposure, but it does not contain a direct, target-period, ruler-attributed existential-risk choice. Most items are treaty, institutional, or conventional-conflict context, so the package cannot fairly present 1B conduct rather than posture."},{"chapter_id":"2B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0001","reason":"Constitutional authority is useful attribution context, but it is not itself a 2022 peace or war decision."},{"evidence_id":"E0016","reason":"Official government framing of hostilities is self-justifying and should not be treated as independent proof of the underlying battlefield cause."},{"evidence_id":"E0018","reason":"Eritrean-troop references are important context, but the article does not establish Abiy's personal command over those forces."},{"evidence_id":"E0021","reason":"Strong atrocity evidence, but it is a commission finding about government forces and allies rather than direct proof of Abiy's own orders."},{"evidence_id":"E0023","reason":"Retrospective synthesis of 2022 conditions; useful, but it blends multiple causes and actors."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Cleaner evidence on who first violated the March ceasefire and how far Abiy personally controlled allied and regional forces.","lenses":["2B.2","2B.5","2B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"AU mediation records, Ethiopian command statements, Eritrea-related reporting, and later investigative/legal findings on ceasefire breaches.","why_it_matters":"Attribution determines whether escalation is ruler-driven or only loosely associated with the government."},{"gap":"Better implementation evidence after the November agreement, especially on access, protection, and compliance.","lenses":["2B.4","2B.7","2B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"UN OCHA/WFP access logs, AU implementation communiques, and contemporaneous field reporting through late 2022 and early 2023.","why_it_matters":"The package shows signature and intent, but less clearly whether peace commitments translated into durable conduct."},{"gap":"More independent evidence on accountability for civilian-harm allegations in Tigray and Oromia.","lenses":["2B.4","2B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"UN expert follow-up, human-rights investigations, or court/inquiry records on airstrikes, siege conditions, and proxy conduct.","why_it_matters":"Without stronger corroboration, the package leans heavily on allegations and retrospective rights synthesis."}],"reason":"The package fairly presents the mixed trajectory: truce, renewed fighting, peace talks, civilian-harm findings, and post-agreement implementation concerns. The remaining problem is attribution clarity, especially around allied forces, ceasefire violations, and whether peace commitments were implemented beyond formal signature."},{"chapter_id":"3B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0001","reason":"Office-power baseline only; it should not be read as evidence of domestic abuse or restraint."},{"evidence_id":"E0035","reason":"This is allegation-heavy reporting on air strikes and should be paired with stronger corroboration before treating it as established fact."},{"evidence_id":"E0036","reason":"Secondary summary of an EHRC report; useful, but the underlying rights-body report would be stronger for attribution and detail."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Direct chain-of-command evidence for regional and allied security-force abuses, especially outside Tigray.","lenses":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"EHRC primary reports, court records, parliamentary inquiries, and command/disciplinary announcements tied to 2022 incidents.","why_it_matters":"The package shows serious harm, but some of the hardest incidents remain only indirectly linked to Abiy."},{"gap":"More independent corroboration for the Oromiya airstrike allegations and for post-truce abuses by allies.","lenses":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"UN or NGO field investigations, satellite/event-data analysis, and hospital/forensic records from affected areas.","why_it_matters":"Several adverse claims are serious but not fully settled in the dossier."},{"gap":"Clearer evidence on remedial action and discipline after abuse allegations.","lenses":["3B.4","3B.5","3B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Official disciplinary files, prosecutor actions, EHRC follow-up, and monitoring reports after the January-February emergency rollback.","why_it_matters":"The package documents harm better than remedy, which weakens the balance for fairness and accountability."}],"reason":"This chapter is substantially stronger than 1B because it combines restraint signals, repression, civilian harm, and accountability failures. It still needs a cleaner evidentiary chain on attribution for some regional or allied abuses, plus stronger corroboration for allegation-heavy items."},{"chapter_id":"4B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0001","reason":"Institutional baseline only; it does not prove political freedom outcomes in 2022."},{"evidence_id":"E0038","reason":"This is mostly 2021-election legacy evidence, so it should be clearly labeled as background rather than 2022 conduct."},{"evidence_id":"E0032","reason":"Useful repression context, but it mixes 2022 conditions with a broader retrospective synthesis."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Direct 2022 evidence of whether Abiy strengthened or weakened independent courts, legislature, and oversight bodies.","lenses":["4B.4","4B.8"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Court-independence reporting, parliamentary records, and appointment/removal decisions from 2022.","why_it_matters":"The package emphasizes coercion and media pressure more than institutional reinforcement or self-binding."},{"gap":"Cleaner separation of the 2021 electoral legacy from actual 2022 ruler conduct.","lenses":["4B.1","4B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Election-observer reports, legal challenges, and 2022 political-rights reporting that isolates the target year.","why_it_matters":"The current record leans on inherited electoral disputes, which can blur 2022 attribution."},{"gap":"More direct evidence on term-limit, succession, and coalition-restraint behavior in 2022.","lenses":["4B.1","4B.8"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Constitutional and party records, coalition agreements, and any 2022 statements on succession or transfer rules.","why_it_matters":"The package is strong on pressure and digital control, weaker on formal contestability and transfer-rule tests."}],"reason":"The package captures a genuine 2022 stall: emergency rollback and dialogue on one side, repression and media pressure on the other. It needs tighter year-specific institutional evidence to distinguish 2022 conduct from inherited electoral and wartime conditions."},{"chapter_id":"5B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0001","reason":"Authority baseline only; it should not be used as economic-performance evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0048","reason":"Retrospective IMF snippet about 2022/23 conditions; useful, but not contemporaneous 2022 evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0049","reason":"Retrospective IMF summary of SOE reform; informative, but it is not a live 2022 assessment."},{"evidence_id":"E0050","reason":"This is a 2023 central-bank statement referencing 2022 inflation, so it should be labeled retrospective."},{"evidence_id":"E0051","reason":"Country-level humanitarian need context, not direct ruler-level economic performance."},{"evidence_id":"E0052","reason":"Post-2022 results brief; helpful context, but it should not be treated as 2022 outcome evidence."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Direct 2022 budget-execution, audit, and implementation evidence for reforms and public-finance management.","lenses":["5B.2","5B.3","5B.5","5B.7"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Ministry of Finance budget-execution reports, auditor-general findings, and IMF/World Bank implementation notes for 2022.","why_it_matters":"The current record is rich in reform intent but thinner on execution quality."},{"gap":"Better household- and region-level distribution evidence, especially for conflict-affected and drought-affected groups.","lenses":["5B.8","5B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Household surveys, poverty updates, and regionally disaggregated humanitarian/economic assessments from 2022.","why_it_matters":"The package can see macro stress, but not as clearly who gained or lost from the ruler's choices."},{"gap":"Stronger evidence on Abiy's personal role in appointing and empowering economic professionals.","lenses":["5B.2","5B.5"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Cabinet appointments, ministry staffing records, and interviews with finance and central-bank officials from 2022.","why_it_matters":"Personal attribution is currently mediated through institutions and advisers."}],"reason":"The package fairly shows mixed economic stewardship: reforms and market openings alongside inflation, FX shortages, conflict spillovers, and humanitarian strain. The main weakness is that several of the strongest items are retrospective or institution-level, so the dossier would benefit from more direct 2022 implementation and distribution evidence."},{"chapter_id":"6B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0051","reason":"This is broad national humanitarian context and should not be treated as direct evidence of Abiy's social-policy choices."},{"evidence_id":"E0053","reason":"Useful program evidence, but donor and partner delivery make ruler attribution partly indirect."},{"evidence_id":"E0063","reason":"Institutional statement about country services and long-run gains; it is not a clean ruler-choice record."},{"evidence_id":"E0067","reason":"System assessment of health financing, useful for context, but not direct evidence of 2022 ruler action."},{"evidence_id":"E0068","reason":"Accessible only as a limited report snippet; it should be treated cautiously as contextual rather than decisive evidence."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"More direct 2022 evidence tying welfare programs to Abiy's own choices rather than UNICEF/WFP/World Bank delivery.","lenses":["6B.1","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Ministry of Health, Education, and Social Affairs budget/execution records; cabinet directives; and independent evaluations of government-led delivery in 2022.","why_it_matters":"The package documents real help, but ruler attribution is often indirect or partner-mediated."},{"gap":"Regionally disaggregated evidence on who benefited from social protection and emergency relief.","lenses":["6B.3","6B.8","6B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Household surveys, subnational nutrition/education access data, and displacement/distribution assessments for 2022.","why_it_matters":"The dossier can show activity, but not always fairness or coverage across groups."},{"gap":"Independent assessment of whether emergency programs produced durable improvements rather than temporary relief.","lenses":["6B.6","6B.9","6B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Program evaluations, audit reports, and follow-up donor assessments into 2023.","why_it_matters":"The record is strong on response, weaker on lasting human-development gains."}],"reason":"The package is balanced and credible: severe need, real government-linked responses, donor dependence, and remaining gaps. The main issue is that many positive items are partner-delivered relief rather than direct Abiy-owned welfare performance."},{"chapter_id":"7B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0001","reason":"Office authority is context only; it does not speak to honesty or self-dealing."},{"evidence_id":"E0039","reason":"Digital repression is relevant to scrutiny and concealment, but it does not by itself prove personal dishonesty."},{"evidence_id":"E0040","reason":"Press-freedom repression is important context, but it is still indirect for personal financial integrity."},{"evidence_id":"E0041","reason":"Detention and due-process failures matter, but they are not proof of personal enrichment or asset conflict."},{"evidence_id":"E0078","reason":"Country press-pressure evidence should be framed as scrutiny obstruction, not as proof of personal benefit."},{"evidence_id":"E0082","reason":"Positive personal-giving narrative is weak evidence for a full integrity conclusion and should be treated cautiously."},{"evidence_id":"E0083","reason":"Official anti-corruption arrests show action, but not independent proof of even-handed enforcement or truthful disclosure."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Audited evidence on Abiy's personal assets, family interests, gifts, or hidden business links.","lenses":["7B.3","7B.4"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Asset declarations, procurement records, investigative audits, and credible financial reporting focused on 2022.","why_it_matters":"The current dossier is strong on media control and anti-corruption rhetoric, but thin on direct self-enrichment evidence."},{"gap":"Better independent evidence on whether anti-corruption and oversight actions were even-handed versus selectively enforced.","lenses":["7B.6","7B.7"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Court records, auditor-general findings, and follow-up reporting on the National Anti-Corruption Committee and PMO-linked projects.","why_it_matters":"The package contains many assertions of action, but not enough proof of neutral enforcement."},{"gap":"More direct evidence on promise-keeping and correction behavior in 2022 beyond wartime and media repression contexts.","lenses":["7B.2","7B.8","7B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Parliamentary transcripts, official corrections, and records of reversals or admissions made after new evidence emerged.","why_it_matters":"The chapter needs a clearer distinction between candor, scapegoating, and political messaging."}],"reason":"This is a plausible integrity dossier, but it is still short on the core personal-nexus proof the chapter needs: assets, conflicts, gifts, and direct personal benefit. It documents scrutiny obstruction and anti-corruption rhetoric well, but not enough independent evidence to settle personal honesty cleanly."},{"chapter_id":"8B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0001","reason":"Executive authority baseline is context, not performance evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0042","reason":"Useful as reform-program context, but it is an IMF staff-visit statement about plans under shocks, not completed execution."},{"evidence_id":"E0046","reason":"Telecom-liberalization planning is real, but the expected investment figures are projections rather than 2022 outcomes."},{"evidence_id":"E0047","reason":"Concrete market opening, but still only partial evidence of broader program execution."},{"evidence_id":"E0071","reason":"Anti-corruption committee launch shows intent and action, but it is still self-reported government activity."},{"evidence_id":"E0073","reason":"Appointment of an auditor-general is helpful, but it is not by itself proof of better governance outcomes."},{"evidence_id":"E0084","reason":"EIH launch is setup and mandate evidence, not demonstrated implementation."},{"evidence_id":"E0085","reason":"Program statement from a senior adviser; useful for revealed intent, but not outcome evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0086","reason":"IMF-described reform package is primarily an announced agenda under external shocks, not proof of success."},{"evidence_id":"E0093","reason":"Anti-corruption committee reporting is official self-presentation and should not be over-read as effective implementation."},{"evidence_id":"E0094","reason":"Auditor-general appointment is relevant, but it needs independent confirmation of effect and autonomy."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"More independent evidence that 2022 reform announcements turned into measurable implementation and outcomes by year-end.","lenses":["8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Independent evaluations, budget execution, telecom rollout data, and SOE performance records through late 2022 and 2023.","why_it_matters":"The package is strong on declared intent and some actions, but weaker on verified output and durability."},{"gap":"Clearer evidence on Abiy's personal management of coordination and bottlenecks inside ministries and SOEs.","lenses":["8B.3","8B.5","8B.8"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Cabinet reshuffles, internal appointment records, and interviews or watchdog reports on implementation disputes.","why_it_matters":"Execution is attributed to the administration, but personal ownership is only partly demonstrated."},{"gap":"More balanced independent sourcing on whether reform institutions like EIH and the auditor-general actually improved discipline versus just creating new structures.","lenses":["8B.4","8B.5","8B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Audit follow-up, parliamentary oversight, and third-party governance assessments.","why_it_matters":"The dossier shows architecture and some movement, but not enough to settle competence at a high level."}],"reason":"The package is rich and coherent on program, reforms, and some implementation, especially telecom opening, SOE restructuring, and the peace-deal rollout. The main weakness is that too much of the evidence is official or retrospective, so the dossier needs stronger independent outcome verification before it can be treated as fully settled."}]}
